newsitem.title: CHILE: El Abra accident cuts output by 9,000 tonnes - paper.
newsitem.headline: El Abra accident cuts output by 9,000 tonnes - paper.

text.p: Chile's El Abra copper mine will produce 58,000 tonnes of copper cathodes this year, 9,000 tonnes less than originally planned, as a result of a serious accident at the pit this month, said evening newspaper La Segunda.

The newspaper, quoting the mine's general manager Johann von Loebenstein, said the pit will now come into full production at the end of November instead of at the start of the month as first scheduled.
El Abra, which cast its first cathode in August, is 51-percent owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals with the rest held by state copper company Codelco.
The pit will be opened officially by President Eduardo Frei Friday.
Von Loebenstein said the mine expects sales this year of $120 million assuming an average copper price of $0.90 a pound.
Four miners died at the pit two weeks ago when a tunnel covering a conveyor belt collapsed burying them under tonnes of rocks and debris.
Mine officials have said the conveyor belt, which links the open-cast pit and the heapleaching plant, should be working again by mid-November.
